main_body: Small orange chest or crate with grey metal corner posts, blue rivets and a dark base with a yellow/black zigzag band
top_band: Light orange rows ~2-3, directly followed by orange plank bands of similar tone (rows 4-9). No distinct top surface, only horizontal plank stripes.
evidence: Reading down the middle column, I find a dark outline, a light orange band of about 2 rows, then more orange horizontal bands in similar tones, then a dark base with a zigzag pattern. The light band is at most 2 rows and has no front-edge line or eave shadow beneath it. It reads as one more plank on a face-on front, not as a lid seen from above. The stripes, rivets and zigzag are all painted flat on a vertical face. This matches the front-elevation failure in the guide.

style.evidence: The orange body is built from a few flat bands of 3-4 tones with almost no grain, speckle or per-plank variation. The outline is dark and mostly neutral around the grey posts and base, so it leans toward the sticker look instead of using the dark tone of each neighbouring material. The metal posts and zigzag base are simple flat fills. Next to the stall and well references, which have 5-6 steps and rich texture, the piece is thinner, flatter and carries fewer colours per tile.
